svg.title: Pelvic pain decision chart: acute pain sorted by beta-hCG, fever and hemoglobin into ovarian torsion or ruptured hemorrhagic cyst; chronic pain sorted by cycle and exam into primary dysmenorrhea or structural causes (endometriosis, adenomyosis, leiomyoma); each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order

svg.text: Pelvic pain: ACUTE (find the life- or limb-threat first) or CHRONIC (≥ 6 MONTHS)?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: history + physical exam come first: the most important part of any approach

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: chronic = below the umbilicus, ≥ 6 months, disabling or needing treatment · up to 50% have experienced abuse or trauma

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: CHRONIC: is it CYCLIC with a NORMAL exam?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: YES → functional (primary) · NO, or an exam/imaging finding → STRUCTURAL (secondary), more common with AGE

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: β-hCG < 1 · afebrile: is the hemoglobin STABLE?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: group and screen · repeat the CBC if bleeding may be ongoing
